question: On which model was the Second Five-Year Plan made?
solution:
The correct answer is the **__PC Mahalanobis model__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Second Five-Year Plan is based on the so-called Mahalanobis model**. This was the** USSR model Indianized by PC Mahalanobis**,** the founder of the Indian Statistical Institute **and close aid of Nehru.
 
• This Model is known to have set the **statistical foundation for state-directed investment **and created the intellectual underpinnings of the** License Raj through an elaborate input-output model**.
 
• This Model suggested that heavy industries should be emphasized, which can lead the Indian economy to a long-term higher growth path.
 
• **India's Second Five-Year Plan and Industrial policy Resolution 1956**, which paved the way for the **Development of the Public Sector and License Raj were based upon this model**.
 
• **The Second Five-Year plan**, based on a **Socialistic pattern, **targeted an increase of 25% in National Income by Rapid Industrialization; however, achieved a target of only **20%**. Further, per capita income grew by** 8%** only.
 
• During this plan **Domestic Production of Industrial products was encouraged**, particularly in the development of the **Public Sector.**
 
• During this Plan Period the **Industry policy resolution was amended **and the primary responsibility for development was left to the **Public Sector**.
 
• The Private Sector was more or less confined to the** Consumer Industries only**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Harrod Domar Model **is a **Keynesian Model of Economic Growth in development economics**, developed by **F. Harrod in 1939 and Evsey Domar in 1946**. This Model focused on understanding **economic instability by analyzing the Dynamic nature of Capital and Investment**.
 
• **Manmohan Plan** abolished** licensing in all industries except a few** of the 18 MRTP companies, which were free from the ceiling limit of assets.** It reduced import barriers** to globalizing the economy, by granting greater autonomy and making management more professional.
 
 
• Features of the Manmohan plan were,
 
 
• **Devaluation of the rupee **was carried out against major Currencies by around **9 percent on 1 July 1991**.
 
• **India's Gold holdings** were pledged with the **Bank of England in four tranches** from **4-18 July 1991 raising around $ 400 million through this route**.
 
 
 
 
 
• The** Planning Commission** of India was an** Institution of the Government of India**. It is a** Non-Constitutional body**, whose main task **was to make Five-Year Plan**. **On 13th August 2014**, the** Planning Commission was abolished **and replaced **by the NITI Aayog**, **effective from Jan 1st, 2015**.
 
• **The fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-79) was also called the 'Investment Model of Planning Commission'**.
 
 
• The 2 main Objectives of this Plan were
 
 
• **Poverty Eradication**.
 
• **Attainment of Self-reliance**.
